answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding reputation to costly, time-delayed work. Rewards stay locked through a vesting tide that only releases after roughly one hundred attested epochs, so mass account creation is expensive. A dishonest node can only ripple its influence outward slowly, while attestation from established non-kin peers checks collusion. As a gale of fake identities sweeps in, requiring cross-verified, non-kin endorsements keeps the network anchored to genuine behavior rather than inflated headcount.
